author: The Bradenton Herald (TNS)
title: Congressional District 16 candidate arrested, records show - NewsBreak
text:
By The Bradenton Herald (TNS) ,
8 hours ago The new congressional district map taking effect for this year's elections. [ LANGSTON TAYLOR | Times ] A candidate for Florida’s 16th Congressional District faces a misdemeanor charge of obstructing without violence, according to Manatee County Jail records.
Deputies arrested Mark Davis, 42, and booked him into the Manatee County Jail on Tuesday, where he was released later the same day after posting a $500 bond, records show.
The first-degree misdemeanor charge applies when someone resists or obstructs an officer performing a lawful duty without using violence, according to Florida law. The charge is punishable by up to a year in jail, up to one year of probation and up to a $1,000 fine.
In his campaign to fill Congressman Vern Buchanan’s seat in Congress, Davis has been a provocative voice in the race. He has amassed 80,000 followers on Facebook, using the account to post profanity-laden messages that criticize political opponents.
Congressional District 16 Incumbent: Vern Buchanan (R)
Florida's 7th largest district by area
Geography
Parts of Pinellas, Manatee, DeSoto, Hardee, Polk, Sarasota and Hillsborough (no residential areas) counties. Includes south St. Petersburg, Bradenton, Arcadia and Wauchula
Politics
How it voted (2024): Trump +13.7
Demographics (all residents)
White: 66%
Hispanic or Latino: 15%
Black or African American: 12%
A year ago, law enforcement officers escorted Davis out of a Gov. Ron DeSantis news conference in Bradenton after he stood during the governor’s remarks and yelled that DeSantis was “bowing down” to a pedophile, seemingly referencing the controversy around the federal government’s Jeffrey Epstein investigation. Davis did not face charges in that incident.
Video details Mark Davis arrest Additional information about Davis’ arrest was not available Wednesday. However, Davis posted video to social media showing deputies at his home serving what a deputy identified as a court order. In the video, Davis reads part of the order stating it authorizes Florida’s Child Protective Investigations to conduct a “safety assessment regarding allegations of abuse, abandonment or neglect.”
In the video, Davis denied any wrongdoing, stating that law enforcement was “harassing his family” and that they were all “happy” and “healthy.” He also repeatedly objected to the search while telling deputies to leave his property, calling them “a bunch of cowboys.”
“I do not consent to this and this is against the law,” Davis said. “You guys are all getting freaking sued. This is ridiculous.”
After Davis stepped toward the house, a deputy stopped him and said, “You’re not going inside, bud.”
Davis asked whether the court order allowed deputies to keep him out of his home before moving toward the deputy, repeatedly saying, “Touch me, touch me, touch me, touch me,” as the deputy extended an arm to stop him. The video ends shortly afterward.
Manatee congressional candidate arrested Reached for comment Wednesday afternoon, Davis responded with a brief statement that again lobbed accusations at President Donald Trump.
Davis also addressed the arrest in a Wednesday morning social media post, where he described officers coming to his home with a court order and searching his home before arresting him.
“They separated me from my family and walked through every room,” Davis wrote, adding that officers “left with nothing” after searching the home. “Then they stood for what felt like forever while I sat in the back of a patrol car.”
Later in the post, Davis alleged the arrest was an attempt to intimidate him over his political campaign.
“You thought you’d scare me into disappearing. Instead, you created the one person who won’t stop until the truth comes out,” Davis said.
On his Facebook page, Davis has posted about other run-ins with law enforcement officers in his neighborhood, suggesting that the deputies were trying to intimidate him.
Davis is running with no party affiliation for the District 16 seat that will be vacated by Buchanan, who announced earlier this year that he would not seek reelection after 20 years in Congress.
According to his campaign website, Davis supports healthcare for all, abortion rights and more restrictive gun control laws.
Florida’s 16th Congressional District includes all or parts of Manatee, Sarasota, Pinellas, DeSoto, Hardee and Polk counties under the new congressional map being used for the 2026 election.
Bradenton Herald reporter Carter Weinhofer contributed to this article.
